newsitem.title: FRANCE: Trichet says EMU participants must meet criteria.
newsitem.headline: Trichet says EMU participants must meet criteria.

text.p: Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet said on Friday he hoped as many countries as possible would be in the first wave of members of the planned single European currency but they would have to meet the Maastricht treaty conditions for monetary union.
"We hope that the European members of the first train... will as numerous as possible on condition they respect the criteria in the (Maastricht) treaty," he told Europe 1 radio.
He was answering a question about whether he hoped Italy and Spain would take part in monetary union from its scheduled start in 1999.
Trichet added he was confident France and Germany would meet the convergence criteria in the treaty, which includes the crucial condition of reducing public deficits to three percent of GDP in 1997.

"Knowing the determination of the French government and of the president (Jacques Chirac), knowing the determination of European governments and naturally of the German government, I'm confident personally," he said in the interview.
Trichet reiterated that conditions were in place for growth in France, saying that low interest rates were especially conducive. "It's the moment now to invest," he said.
He added long-term interest rates had fallen to a 78-year low and that official rates were "exceptionally low".
